Posted May 17, 2001
(MarijuanaNews note: The op-ed below is one of the most vicious and deceitful pieces that I have seen in a long time. The author led the opposition to last year’s marijuana legalization initiative in Alaska, so he is not new to this. The Anchorage Daily News is prohibitionist, but it should have some standards about what it will print. Clearly, they do not.

I have responded to a variety of Shea’s more general -- and hysterical – allegations by providing links to the facts.

However, the most pernicious lies here are gross misrepresentations of the

As we will see, whoever mined this data had to know that he was lying. Perhaps Shea simply thought that no one would actually look at the DAWN data. Perhaps he thinks that the Anchorage Daily News will not care, and will not print any rebuttal. It will be interesting to see if they care about the truth.)

From The Anchorage Daily News

By Wevley Shea, " Anchorage attorney and former United States Attorney for the District of Alaska. "

DRUGS ATTACK SOCIETY'S MORAL FIBER

Compass

The pro-drug legalization movement in Alaska and worldwide received a strong setback on May 10. President George W. Bush nominated John P. Walters to be his Director of National Drug Control Policy. Mr. Walters is a very experienced drug warrior. President Bush and Mr. Walters strongly oppose drug legalization.
See
The Narking of America: The Bush Team for Total War, or Just to Keep the Lid On.

The moral foundation of our nation is founded on free, independent thinking. The ability to distinguish right from wrong and individual responsibility form the basis for our democratic republic.
(MarijuanaNews note: Does the " ability to distinguish right from wrong " include knowing the difference between truth and lies? Does " individual responsibility " include being responsible for the consequences of lying?)

Drugs destroy the ability to be free and think independently. The drug legalization movement in Alaska is targeting our children.
(MarijuanaNews note: That is a blood libel. In any case, it would be absurd for any reform movement to " target children " who cannot vote.)
See
Remarkable Statement By Jamaican Clergy Calling For Legalization of Ganja.

The youth of Alaska need to know drugs are harmful.

Alaska, over the past few years, has been a specific target for the drug legalization movement. The leaders of this movement are from outside Alaska and are financed by individuals from outside Alaska. Alaskans are unique, independent free thinkers. Drugs destroy all that Alaskans hold dear.
See
We Are Still Winning! Almost A Third of DEAland " Agree that Marijuana Should Be Legalized. " Okay, But More Than That Voted for Legalization Plus in Alaska.

Most specifically, drugs destroy families and the true victims are our children.
See
Family Of Malibu Millionaire Murdered In 1992 By Narks Trying to Steal His Ranch Will Be Given $5 Million Because Officials " feared jurors would not believe government agents. "
and
Sioux Family Devastated By DEA Destruction of Hemp Crop. Predators Victimizing the Most Vulnerable.

Drug legalization, if allowed, will destroy democracy as we know it.
and
Legalize Marijuana and Reduce Use?
New Survey Puts Estimate of Dutch Marijuana Use Even More Below DEAland
and
Drug Czar Lies Again About the Dutch, Who Respond With The Facts;
Czar’s Aid Says, " forces at work to legalize drugs are trying to bring
these wonderfully allied governments into conflict. "
and
The Drug Czar’s Testimony On " The Drug Legalization Movement In America " Has Three Parts:Lie About The Anti-Prohibitionist Movement; Lie About Marijuana; Lie About The Netherlands. With A Little Lying About Me.

Alaskans have been misled to believe that the use of marijuana is safe. The dopers argue that marijuana is a " medicine. "
See
Paranoia and the Party Line on Medical Marijuana. Who Do They Think They Are Fooling? The DEA and Bob Barr.

The dopers want to " smoke marijuana, " a weed with more cancer-causing agents than tobacco.
See
High anxieties: What the WHO doesn't want you to know about cannabis Health officials in Geneva have suppressed the publication of a politically sensitive analysis that confirms what ageing hippies have known for decades: cannabis is safer than alcohol or tobacco.
and
The Reality Of the Marijuana Situation In Canada: Unequal Injustice.
Alcohol Costs Canadian Health Almost 100 Times As Much As Marijuana.
Tobacco: Almost 200 As Much – Article and Editorial
and
Criminologist Defends Constable’s Call For Legal Marijuana:
" Alcohol and tobacco much more harmful than cannabis. "

This marijuana has no quality-control standards and no quality-control dosages. Quite simply it is street dope.
(MarijuanaNews note: There is no quality control for contraband, which is an argument for – not against – marijuana legalization.)

However, the marijuana raised in some of Alaska's quality indoor hydroponic operations is very strong. It is 20 to 50 times stronger that the '60s dope of Haight Ashbury in San Francisco.
(MarijuanaNews note: First, there is no data from the " '60s dope of Haight Ashbury " – or anywhere else. Large-scale testing did not begin until the late 1970s.

Second, there has been no change in average marijuana potency in 20 years.

Third, potency is irrelevant, because stronger marijuana is safer, inasmuch as people smoke less.)

In 1999 a survey of 134 hospital emergency room departments confirmed the addictive destruction of marijuana.

According to the Drug Abuse Warning Network, marijuana/hashish was the second most frequently mentioned illicit drug addressed in the survey.

Marijuana/hashish emergency department cases in San Francisco increased 121% in the first half of 2000.

Those individuals treated for marijuana/hashish addressed why they sought emergency treatment: 14,790 were treated for unexpected reactions; 9,072 for overdoses; 7,737 were seeking detoxification and 15,636 confirmed they were dependent on it.

This study was of only 134 emergency departments. Imagine the true scope of the problem.

Medical examiners in the study confirmed 670 individuals lost their lives due to marijuana in 1999.

Second, to give Shea credit for the one thing that is correct here, but which he does not seem to understand – or care about – he initially uses the correct word, " mentions. " This means that these episodes involve " mentions " of various drugs, not necessarily the causes of the trip to the emergency rooms. However, he quickly changes the terminology.

Yes, there was a 121% increase in emergency room mentions – not cases – in San Francisco, but his choice of San Francisco data was obviously intended to deceive, because the DAWN report clearly states, " Marijuana/hashish mentions remained stable nationwide between the first half of 1999 and the first half of 2000…) ".

Moreover, the DAWN report says, " When reported as DAWN ED mentions, marijuana/hashish is likely to be mentioned in combination with other substances, particularly alcohol and cocaine. "

The DAWN report says " up to 5 drugs can be reported for each drug abuse episode. "

In fact, roughly 78% of DAWN ED mentions of marijuana/hashish involve other drugs. There were only around 19,000 emergency room marijuana-only mentions.

To put this in context, there were over 90 million emergency room visits in 1999 for all reasons. Of those, only around 550,000 involved all of the illicit drugs, and one third of those involved " alcohol-in combination " with some illicit drug. Marijuana mentions accounted for less than 90,000 in all of 1999.

The marijuana-only " mentions " account for only 19,000 out 90 million emergency room visits. Does that sound like a major health threat?

To offer a little further perspective, there were over 50,000 mentions of aspirin, acetaminophen and ibuprofen.

It is also important to note that the DAWN report says " that alcohol is reported to DAWN only when present in combination with another reportable drug. "

That is, the DAWN program does not deal with alcohol related emergency room visits -- except when alcohol is used with an illegal drug. Clearly, this program was designed to generate data to support the drug war.

Nonetheless, " alcohol-in-combination was mentioned in 33 percent (97,143) of ED drug episodes in the first half of 2000. " That means that " alcohol-in-combination " was the largest single category, roughly twice the annual number of mentions as marijuana.

Regarding Shea’s claim that " individuals treated for marijuana/hashish addressed why they sought emergency treatment: 14,790 were treated for unexpected reactions; 9,072 for overdoses; 7,737 were seeking detoxification and 15,636 confirmed they were dependent on it. " –

Notice that the term " mentions " has disappeared. Now these are " individuals treated for marijuana/hashish. " However, they were not " treated for marijuana/hashish. " In 78% of the visits they had mentioned marijuana in combination with other substances, particularly " alcohol and cocaine. " So, if someone visits the emergency room to be treated for problems with alcohol or cocaine – or whatever – and say that they need detoxification or treatment for dependence on the " other substances, " then that need for treatment is noted in the column by all of the " mentions " -- including marijuana.

Regarding Shea’s claim that " This study was of only 134 emergency departments. Imagine the true scope of the problem. " --

He seems to be trying to create the impression that the problem must be vast. Well, one need not rely on the imagination. The 2000 DAWN report specifically says, " From January to June 2000, DAWN estimates that there were 292,098 drug-related ED episodes in the coterminous U.S. with 535,646 drug mentions. "

Regarding Shea’s claim that " Medical examiners in the study confirmed 670 individuals lost their lives due to marijuana in 1999. " –

Again, the DAWN data does not say that marijuana caused the deaths.

The

The deaths were the result of something else and marijuana was mentioned as having also been used. Even Shea should know that there is no lethal dose of marijuana.

The above quotes and data from the DAWN reports make very clear that marijuana is not the cause of significant public health problems. It is quite clear that Shea has completely misrepresented the DAWN data in away that could not be the result of any misunderstanding. This has to be deliberate. He is a vicious liar.)

Marijuana is a gateway drug that the legalizers are using in an attempt to legalize otherillegal drugs.
(MarijuanaNews note: From the Institute of Medicine report on medical marijuana-- " Patterns in progression of drug use from adolescence to adulthood are strikingly regular. Because it is the most widely used illicit drug, marijuana is predictably the first illicit drug most people encounter. Not surprisingly, most users of other illicit drugs have used marijuana first. In fact, most drug users begin with alcohol and nicotine before marijuana -- usually before they are of legal age…

In the sense that marijuana use typically precedes rather than follows initiation of other illicit drug use, it is indeed a " gateway " drug. But because underage smoking and alcohol use typically precede marijuana use, marijuana is not the most common, and is rarely the first, " gateway " to illicit drug use. There is no conclusive evidence that the drug effects of marijuana are causally linked to the subsequent abuse of other illicit drugs. "

Marijuana is merely the first step on the path to legalization.
See
Isn't legalizing marijuana just the opening wedge to legalizing all drugs?

The outspoken leadership of President Bush and Mr. Walters is absolutely necessary in combating the effect of illegal drug trafficking in Alaska and worldwide. The basic drug message for our children is quite simple: If we allow our President and national leadership to send a permissive drug message, drug use goes up drastically.

We are not losing the Drug War. Setbacks have occurred and lessons learned. Drug legalization should not be tolerated. In 1979, with 25 million drug users, our nation demanded changes. By 1992 the number of drug users was down to 12 million due to the leadership of President Ronald Reagan and President George Bush responding to very concerned citizens. Parents nationwide lead the attack on illicit drug usage. By
1999 the number of drug users had increased to 15 million due to very permissive leadership in Washington.
See
NORML Reports: In 1999, A New Record for Marijuana Arrests! 4,175,357 Americans Have Been Arrested During the Clinton Administration.

Like World War II, our continuing " War on Drugs " is for the moral fiber of the free world, our nation, and the future of our children.

Drug traffickers and dealers are the " Hitlers " of today. These individuals are " one step up from child molesters " and should be condemned. If illegal drugs are allowed to be socially acceptable, future generations of children will never have a chance. Drugs destroy the moral fiber of our society.
(MarijuanaNews note: I think that such lies and hatred are doing more to " destroy the moral fiber of our society " than any substances ever could.)

Our elected officials, local, state and federal law enforcement/prosecutors and each concerned Alaskan should openly oppose illicit drug legalization.
(MarijuanaNews note: Should they lie when they do so?

If marijuana is so damned dangerous, why do people like Shea have to lie about it? Do the editors of the Anchorage Daily Mail care that they have been used by a former federal prosecutor to lie to their readers? And will anyone note that in the context of his moral pretensions he has violated the Commandment against giving false witness against his neighbors, the marijuana users of Alaska -- and opponents of marijuana prohibition everywhere?

I hope as many people as possible write to the ADN editors to complain about these lies.)
